typeData.name: 22V10
typeData.behavior:
; 22V574 — 8-bit register with synchronous clear, load enable, output
; enable, and asynchronous set/reset.
;
; ALL FIVE CONTROL PINS ARE ACTIVE LOW, which is what their leading '/'
; records (renamed 2026-07-31; they were CLR/EN/OE/SET/RST, whose names
; read active-high while the equations below have always been active-low):
;   /CLR  LOW  clears the register synchronously, at the next clock edge
;   /EN   LOW  loads D at the clock edge; HIGH holds the current value
;   /OE   LOW  enables the Q outputs; HIGH floats them
;   /RST  LOW  clears the register asynchronously (GALasm global AR)
;   /SET  LOW  presets the register asynchronously (GALasm global SP)
;
; Equations are physical-level GALasm (design §7.6): a signal name is the
; pin name with any leading '/' dropped, so the '/' above is documentation
; and these equations are unchanged by the rename. A bare signal means
; "that pin reads HIGH", a slashed one "that pin reads LOW" — so
; `CLR * /EN * Dn` loads Dn while /CLR is high (not clearing) and /EN is
; low (load enabled), and `CLR * EN * Qn` holds while both pins are high.
; With /CLR low both terms vanish and the register clocks in zeros.
;
; SEQUENTIAL-PART CLOCK CONVENTION: GALasm's .R outputs are clocked by the
; GAL22V10's dedicated pin-1 clock, a role played here by CLK (rising
; edge). CLK therefore appears in no equation; the .R suffix implies it.
Q0.R = CLR * /EN * D0
     + CLR *  EN * Q0
Q1.R = CLR * /EN * D1
     + CLR *  EN * Q1
Q2.R = CLR * /EN * D2
     + CLR *  EN * Q2
Q3.R = CLR * /EN * D3
     + CLR *  EN * Q3
Q4.R = CLR * /EN * D4
     + CLR *  EN * Q4
Q5.R = CLR * /EN * D5
     + CLR *  EN * Q5
Q6.R = CLR * /EN * D6
     + CLR *  EN * Q6
Q7.R = CLR * /EN * D7
     + CLR *  EN * Q7

Q0.E = /OE
Q1.E = /OE
Q2.E = /OE
Q3.E = /OE
Q4.E = /OE
Q5.E = /OE
Q6.E = /OE
Q7.E = /OE

AR   = /RST
SP   = /SET

typeData.name: 22V10
typeData.behavior:
/ENF =  F0*!F1*!F2
     + !F0*F1*!F2
     +  F0*F1*!F2
     + !F0*!F1*F2; update PC when F code is 1..4
OSA  = F0*F1 ; 0 unless F code is 3 or 7 (7 is X)
OSB = !F0*F0 ; always 0 or X
S0 =   !F0*F1*!F2
     + F0*F1*!F2
     +!F0*!F1*F2
S1 =   !F0*F1*!F2
     +  F0*F1*!F2
     + !F0*!F1*F2
S2 = F0 * !F0 ; always zero for now
Cin = !F0* F1*!F2
/BEN = !F0 * !F1 * F2 + F0*F1*!F2
/ZEN = !F0*F1
